countries.reasoning: China dominates rare earth production including Yttrium with around 13,000 metric tons annually, based on USGS 2023 and industry data; very reliable given consistent production figures and government reports.
The US produces Yttrium primarily from Mountain Pass mine; USGS 2023 confirms around 1,700 metric tons, well documented but production is significantly less than China.
India has notable rare earth elements production; figures from national mineral reports and USGS indicate around 1,100 metric tons but exact Yttrium separations less documented.
Australia is a growing supplier of rare earth elements, including Yttrium, with production confirmed near 850 metric tons per year by USGS 2022 data.
Myanmar's production is less well documented and more informal, but estimates suggest around 700 metric tons per year; confidence moderate due to data gaps and political instability.
